title: Modules of finite type and of finite presentation on a ringed space
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space and $\mathcal F$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an open $U\subseteq X$ write $\mathcal O_U=\mathcal O_X|_U$ and $\mathcal F|_U$ for the $\mathcal O_U$-module $W\mapsto\mathcal F(W)$ ($W\subseteq U$ open), and $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$ for the free $\mathcal O_U$-module with basis sections $e_1,\dots,e_n$; sections $s_1,\dots,s_n\in\mathcal F(U)$ determine the $\mathcal O_U$-linear map $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_U$, $e_i\mapsto s_i$, and every $\mathcal O_U$-linear map $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_U$ is of this form. (1) $\mathcal F$ is *of finite type* if every $x\in X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ with finitely many sections $s_1,\dots,s_n\in\mathcal F(U)$ ($n\ge0$) whose map $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_U$ is an epimorphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules ($\mathcal F|_U$ is generated by finitely many sections). (2) $\mathcal F$ is *of finite presentation* if every $x\in X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$, integers $n,m\ge0$ and an $\mathcal O_U$-linear map $\alpha:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$ such that $\mathcal F|_U$ is isomorphic, as an $\mathcal O_U$-module, to the cokernel of $\alpha$ in the category of $\mathcal O_U$-modules.
